evals.prompt: Add annotation-driven OpenAPI documentation to this Maven Mu Server 2.4.1 application. Use mu-swagger 0.1.1 and Swagger Core's Jakarta integration 2.2.54. Preserve Java 21, port 8189, the existing direct MuServerBuilder startup, singleton resource, and GET /hello/{name} behavior. Document the operation, path parameter, and 200 response with io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations; set the API title to Greeting API and version to 1.0.0; expose and verify both JSON and YAML documents. Do not bundle a Swagger UI or add a JSON body provider that this plain-text API does not need.
evals.expected_output: The existing application runs unchanged with its singleton route, while mu-swagger generates parseable /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml documents containing the requested Swagger annotation metadata and API information.
assertions: The project builds and runs on Java 21 with io.muserver:mu-server 2.4.1, io.muserver:mu-swagger 0.1.1, and io.swagger.core.v3:swagger-jaxrs2-jakarta 2.2.54.
The existing direct MuServerBuilder architecture, singleton GreetingResource instance, port 8189, and GET /hello/{name} plain-text behavior are preserved.
The same application resource collection is passed to RestHandlerBuilder and MuOpenApiResourceBuilder, and the built MuOpenApiResource is added to that REST handler.

The resource uses io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations for an operation summary, path-parameter description, and 200 response description; no legacy io.swagger.annotations or javax Swagger/JAX-RS artifact is introduced.
GET /openapi.json returns 200 application/json that parses and contains title Greeting API, version 1.0.0, /hello/{name}, the annotated summary and parameter, and the documented 200 response.
GET /openapi.yaml returns 200 application/yaml with the same intentional document content, and GET /hello/Daniel still returns 200 text/plain with Hello, Daniel.
No Swagger UI assets, UI dependency, dependency-injection framework, or unnecessary application JSON body provider is added.

evals.prompt: Our Mu Server Jakarta REST service has no Swagger annotations and we only need an OpenAPI document that an existing Swagger UI can render. Should we add mu-swagger? Give the smallest direct RestHandlerBuilder configuration, explain UI and CORS responsibilities, and say when mu-swagger would become appropriate.
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to use Mu Server's built-in OpenAPI JSON for an annotation-free service, with Swagger UI kept separate and CORS enabled only for a genuinely cross-origin UI.
assertions: It recommends Mu Server's built-in withOpenApiJsonUrl rather than adding mu-swagger or Swagger Core solely for a Swagger UI.
It shows the existing RestHandlerBuilder retaining the application's resources and adding an OpenAPI JSON URL; the optional Mu read-only HTML URL is distinguished from Swagger UI.
It explains that Swagger UI is separate and can consume the built-in JSON document.
It states that same-origin UI access needs no CORS and that a cross-origin UI should receive a narrowly scoped allowed origin and only required headers.
It notes that the built-in generator does not interpret Swagger Core annotations, so mu-swagger becomes appropriate if that requirement is later introduced.

evals.prompt: This Mu Server app exposes /openapi.json with RestHandlerBuilder.withOpenApiJsonUrl, but summaries from io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations.Operation never appear. We want to keep those Swagger Core annotations. Diagnose the cause and give the minimum migration to mu-swagger, including Java and dependency checks, resource registration, document endpoints, and verification. The application already has a separately hosted Swagger UI.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis that Mu's built-in generator does not consume Swagger Core annotations, followed by a focused migration to the Java-compatible Jakarta mu-swagger integration without adding or confusing it with Swagger UI.
assertions: It identifies the generator mismatch: withOpenApiJsonUrl is Mu Server's built-in generator and does not interpret io.swagger.v3.oas.annotations.
It checks the selected mu-swagger release's Java bytecode requirement and notes that version 0.1.1 requires Java 21.
It keeps the application's direct Mu Server dependency and adds exact compatible mu-swagger and swagger-jaxrs2-jakarta dependencies without switching to javax or legacy io.swagger.annotations.
It passes the same singleton resource instances to RestHandlerBuilder and MuOpenApiResourceBuilder, adds the resulting MuOpenApiResource, and avoids a duplicate built-in /openapi.json route.
It identifies /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml as generated-document endpoints and verifies status, media type, parseability, annotated content, and an unchanged application endpoint.
It does not add Swagger UI because the UI is already separate, and treats CORS, JSON body providers, and authentication as independent runtime concerns.

evals.prompt: This Mu Server 3 service already exposes the intended OpenAPI document at /openapi.json. Host Swagger UI in the same application with Mu Server's WebJar support. Give the Swagger UI group ID and artifact ID, use the current stable release, mount the UI at /api-docs, ensure it loads this service's document rather than the bundled example, and explain version resolution and CORS. Do not replace the existing OpenAPI generator or add Swagger annotations.
evals.expected_output: A same-origin Swagger UI hosted from the org.webjars:swagger-ui dependency under /api-docs, with an application initializer that selects /openapi.json and no change to the existing document generator.
assertions: It adds an exact stable org.webjars:swagger-ui dependency and identifies org.webjars as the group ID and swagger-ui as the artifact ID.
It mounts ResourceHandlerBuilder.webjarHandler("swagger-ui") under ContextHandlerBuilder.context("/api-docs") and identifies /api-docs/index.html as the UI entry page.
It overrides swagger-initializer.js before the WebJar handler so the UI loads /openapi.json rather than the stock Petstore document.
It explains that the one-argument handler reads Maven metadata and that an explicit artifact version can be supplied when multiple versions are present.
It keeps the existing OpenAPI generator and states that WebJar-hosted Swagger UI works with either Mu's built-in document or mu-swagger output without requiring Swagger annotations.
It states that same-origin UI access needs no CORS and does not add a permissive CORS policy.
